title: Technical English — Course 3, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 9

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. Where will the documentation session take place?
tasks.audioText: The CNC documentation session will take place on Friday at nine forty in the computer classroom. Students will review a sample programme sheet, a machine manual extract and a revision record. The instructor will explain why the programme version and equipment reference should be recorded together. The lesson is based on reading documents, not operating machinery.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which record will students review?
tasks.audioText: The CNC documentation session will take place on Friday at nine forty in the computer classroom. Students will review a sample programme sheet, a machine manual extract and a revision record. The instructor will explain why the programme version and equipment reference should be recorded together. The lesson is based on reading documents, not operating machinery.

tasks.prompt: A CNC programme document should be linked to the correct machine and approved revision. If a programme is updated, the revision record explains what changed and when the update was made. This information helps staff avoid confusing an old copy with the current approved version. Students should read the programme in context and use the relevant machine documentation for explanations of controller-specific functions. Reading 1. What does a revision record explain?
options: Which operator used the machine and on what shift
Who approved the purchase and when it was delivered
What changed and when the update was made
How many components were stored in the workshop

tasks.prompt: Why should the programme be linked to the correct machine?
options: To reduce the number of programme lines
To identify the supplier of the controller
To replace the machine's operating instructions
To avoid confusing versions and account for controller-specific functions

tasks.prompt: The programme version ___ in the revision record.
Choose TWO details that support controlled CNC documentation.
options: A personal nickname for the machine

tasks.prompt: A recorded change to a document or programme is a ___.
You find two copies of a programme with different revision numbers. What should you do?
options: Use the newest-looking file without checking.
Check the approved revision record and machine reference before relying on a copy.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of CNC documentation in a logical order.
options: Identify the machine and controller reference
Use the approved documentation for interpretation
correctOrder: Identify the machine and controller reference
Use the approved documentation for interpretation

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining why CNC programme documents need clear revision and machine references. Do not include machine-specific operating instructions.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: the response explains why CNC programme documents need revision and machine/controller references (0–2); it describes checking the current approved document and applicability before relying on it, without giving machine-specific operating instructions (0–2); ideas are clearly connected with understandable grammar (0–2); CNC/document-control vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are accurate (0–2).
